lq.ANSWER: The Economics of Happiness practice session helps us examine the prevailing worldview and its impact on society. The session uses a documentary on the impact of globalisation on Ladakh and asks us to observe the goal of society, the achievements and side effects of the prevalent worldview, and whether there is a solution to present-day problems. The main learning is that development should not be measured only by economic growth, consumption or physical facility. If society focuses only on material growth, it may create side effects such as loss of relationship, cultural breakdown, environmental damage and dissatisfaction. True development must support happiness, prosperity, right relationship, right utilisation and harmony with nature.
